*Prototype instance of [Problem Solution Ladder](../course_design/activities_assessments.md#problem-solution-ladder). Matches [LangChain — Long-term memory](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/long-term-memory).*

## Industry Problem

<!--
  instructor: Cold-call for a personal "I had to re-explain myself" story
  (hotel, airline, support line) — ~1 min, don't let it become a gripe
  session. Land this: they already have short-term memory from Day 1_1
  (thread history). Today's gap is specifically that it dies with the thread.
-->

A hotel concierge agent chats with a returning guest. Last visit, the guest mentioned they're allergic to shellfish and always request a late checkout. Today's conversation is a brand-new thread — a plain agent with only short-term (conversation) memory has already forgotten all of it, and the guest has to repeat themselves every stay.

## Instructor example / demonstration

<!--
  instructor: Live-code this — don't paste a finished cell. The moment that
  sells the competency is running store.put in one cell, then store.get in a
  fresh cell/kernel and having it still resolve. Say out loud: "notice I
  haven't touched the agent yet — this is just a dictionary that survives."
  Prereq: only needs 1_1's API key setup; nothing new to install.
-->

Here's the fix: give the agent a `store` — memory that lives outside any one conversation, per LangChain's long-term memory pattern.

```python
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langgraph.store.memory import InMemoryStore

# InMemoryStore saves data to an in-memory dictionary; a DB-backed store is used in production
store = InMemoryStore()

agent = create_agent(
    "google_genai:gemini-2.5-flash",
    tools=[],
    store=store,
)
```

Watch what happens when a guest preference is written straight into the store, keyed by namespace `(guest_id, "preferences")`, and then read back from a completely separate call — it survives across threads/sessions, unlike short-term memory.

```python
namespace = ("guest-482", "preferences")
store.put(namespace, "dietary", {"note": "Shellfish allergy"})
store.put(namespace, "checkout", {"note": "Always requests late checkout"})

item = store.get(namespace, "dietary")
print(item.value)
```

## Run It Yourself

<!--
  instructor: ~10 min. Circulate for the two most common snags: (1) they name
  the tool parameter `store` instead of using `runtime.store` — flag it
  immediately, it's the #1 error the docs warn about; (2) they forget the
  namespace tuple has to match exactly between put and get. Don't rescue too
  fast — let them hit the KeyError once.
-->

Run the snippet above yourself. Then write a tool that lets your *agent* read from the store via `runtime.store` (per [Long-term memory](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/long-term-memory)), and confirm it can answer *"Any dietary notes for guest-482?"* correctly — in a brand-new conversation thread.

## odify It, Build It

<!--
  instructor: ~15 min, pairs. Good work looks like: a new namespace they
  chose themselves, a tool with a docstring specific enough the agent calls
  it unprompted, and a live demo where a preference mentioned mid-chat is
  still there after starting a new thread. Have partners try to break each
  other's tool before moving on.
-->

Pick a preference the demo tool doesn't cover — room temperature, pillow type, anything you'd want remembered — and build both a namespace and a tool that *writes* it to the store mid-conversation. If a guest mentions it once, your agent should never need to ask again.
